name: I tried an AI tool before and it produced generic results—how do I avoid repeating that mistake?
description: Diagnose the failure before switching tools. Check the audience definition, source material, instructions, quality criteria, integrations, and buyer expectation

mainEntity.name: I tried an AI tool before and it produced generic results—how do I avoid repeating that mistake?

acceptedAnswer.text:
A bad prior experience usually means the next offer needs tighter scope, clearer acceptance criteria, and stronger review—not simply a different AI brand. Identify whether the failure came from poor data, unclear instructions, unreliable output, missing integration, weak demand, or unrealistic expectations.

Context: Run My AI Business emphasizes customization, source verification, approval checkpoints, and iterative refinement. Those controls help distinguish a prompt problem from a business-model or implementation problem.

Key factors:
- What specifically failed
- Whether the process had an accountable owner
- How quality was measured
- What the customer expected to receive

Practical guidance: Rebuild one small workflow with a defined input, output, reviewer, and test sample. Compare the new result against the old process before committing to a broader rollout.

The educational material supports diagnosis and learning rather than promising that any tool will correct every prior issue.
